learningObjective: State the online softmax update rules that let a single-pass streaming algorithm compute exact softmax over a partitioned row.

canonicalClaims.claim: Online softmax merges two partial (max, denominator) states (m_t, d_t) and (m', d') into (m_{t+1}, d_{t+1}) where m_{t+1} = max(m_t, m') and d_{t+1} = d_t * exp(m_t - m_{t+1}) + d' * exp(m' - m_{t+1}).
conditions: Both partial sums use the safe-softmax convention (subtract the local max).
Rescale factors are applied to both partial sums when the global max moves.
nonImplications: Does not imply the algorithm avoids all rounding artifacts.
Does not imply online softmax always outperforms two-pass softmax on all hardware; it primarily wins when re-reading the row is expensive.

misconceptions.claim: Running max is combined by summation: m_{t+1} = m_t + m'.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Max is not additive; it is an elementwise maximum.

misconceptions.claim: Denominators can be summed directly without rescaling because both are 'already normalized'.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are normalized to different local maxes; the sums use different reference points and cannot be added.

misconceptions.claim: Only the new tile needs a rescale; the running sum is authoritative.
misconceptions.whyWrong: If the new tile has a larger max, the old running sum needs to be re-referenced to the new max via exp(m_t - m_{t+1}) <= 1.

implementationFacts: In FlashAttention, this recurrence also carries the running output O_t through the same rescale factor.
Rescale factors are always <= 1 because both m_t and m' <= m_{t+1}.
performanceScenarios: Enables single-pass attention over long sequences without materializing the full attention matrix in HBM.
